glosses.notes: Used for doing something while the time, chance, or favorable condition is still there.

examples.sentence: 我们趁博物馆刚开门、人还不多，先去看里面那个地方，免得过一会门口排队的人越来越多。
她趁领导去外地开会的两天，把已经改了三次的方案又从头细看了一遍，终于发现问题还是出在时间上。
司机趁前面的红灯还有几十秒，赶紧提醒最后几位乘客上车，后面一站人更多，车门就更挤了。

example_translations.translation: We took advantage of the museum just opening and there still not being many people to go see the section inside first, so the line at the entrance would not get longer a little later.

While the director was away in another city for meetings for two days, she went through the proposal from the beginning again even though she had revised it three times, and finally realized the problem was still in the timing.

With only a few dozen seconds left on the red light ahead, the driver hurried to remind the last few passengers to board, because the next stop would have even more people and the doors would get more crowded.

glosses.notes: Can mean physically holding something up or open, and by extension keeping something going under pressure.

examples.sentence: 临时舞台后面的板太高，工作人员只好用两根木头从后面撑住，大家才敢继续把灯和字往上挂。
院子里的花快倒了，父亲拿一根木头把它从旁边撑住，还叫孩子明天再给下面加一点土。
这家小书店最难的时候，全靠老板晚上另外接翻译工作来撑着，才没有在那条街改之前就先关门。

example_translations.translation: The board behind the temporary stage was too tall, so the staff had to prop it up from behind with two pieces of wood before everyone dared keep hanging the lights and lettering higher.
The flowers in the yard were about to fall over, so the father used a piece of wood to prop them up from the side and told the child to add a little more soil underneath the next day.
At its hardest time, this little bookstore survived only because the owner took on translation work at night, and that kept it from shutting down before the street was redone.

glosses.notes: A name or title given to someone because of their role, ability, achievements, or reputation.

examples.sentence: 他在单位里干了二十多年，不爱说大话，却总能把最麻烦的事处理好，所以大家一直把这个称号送给他。
那位老教师退休很多年以后，学校还是常在介绍里保留她的称号，因为一提到她，几代学生都还记得。
队里给新人发奖时没有乱起称号，而是先问大家愿不愿意接受这样的叫法，免得本来想让大家高兴，反而让人不舒服。

example_translations.translation: He had worked there for more than twenty years and never liked bragging, yet he could always handle the hardest problems well, so everyone kept giving him that title.
Even many years after the old teacher retired, the school still kept her title in its introductions, because several generations of students still remembered her as soon as she was mentioned.

When the team gave awards to newcomers, they did not casually invent titles, but first asked whether everyone was willing to accept that kind of label, so that what was meant to make people happy would not make anyone uncomfortable instead.

glosses.notes: Can mean addressing someone in a certain way or the name or title used when doing so.

examples.sentence: 第一次去对方那边开会时，他先问秘书见到那位负责人应该怎么称呼，怕自己一开口就不合适。
孩子刚去幼儿园的时候，总把女老师都只称呼成老师，后来才慢慢学会按姓来分。
在这个村子里，大家对长辈的称呼分得很细，差一代或者换一家亲戚，说法就不一样。

example_translations.translation: The first time he went there for a meeting, he first asked the secretary how he should address the person in charge, worried that the moment he opened his mouth he might sound inappropriate.
When the child had just started kindergarten, he kept addressing all the female teachers simply as “teacher,” and only later slowly learned to distinguish them by surname.
In this village, the forms of address for elders are divided very finely. If you are off by one generation or the family connection changes, the wording changes too.

glosses.notes: Used when something or someone is referred to by a certain name, label, or description.

examples.sentence: 这片老街原来只是码头边的旧房子，后来因为聚集了很多修船的人，才慢慢被外地人称作码头街。
医生说这种反应不能简单称作过敏，因为它不是一下出现的，而是药长期积累以后才慢慢显出来。
把临时的让步称作真正的解决办法还太早，因为最核心的问题一点也没有减少。

example_translations.translation: This old street had originally just been a cluster of old houses by the dock. Later, because many ship repairers gathered there, people from out of town gradually started calling it Dock Street.
The doctor said this reaction could not simply be called an allergy, because it did not appear all at once but only slowly showed up after the medicine had built up over time.
It is too early to call this temporary concession a real solution, because the central problem has not lessened at all.

glosses.notes: A measure word for one tenth, often used for percentages, proportions, and rates such as 七成 or 九成.

examples.sentence: 演出消息刚放出来的时候，剧院网站不到半天就卖掉了七成的票，连组织的人自己都没想到外地观众会来得这么快。
这家店重新装修以后，老顾客已经回来了八成，店长还是天天站在门口看大家最先往哪边走。
讨论了两个小时以后，参加会议的人里有九成同意先试行三个月，因为谁也不想让计划一直停在纸面上。

example_translations.translation: When the performance announcement first came out, the theater website sold seven tenths of the tickets in less than half a day, and even the organizers themselves had not expected people from other places to come so quickly.
After the shop was renovated, eighty percent of the old customers had already come back, yet the manager still stood at the door every day watching which way people headed first.
After two hours of discussion, ninety percent of the people at the meeting agreed to try the plan for three months first, because no one wanted to keep the proposal sitting on paper forever.

glosses.notes: A formal verb for taking a vehicle such as a bus, train, plane, or shuttle.

examples.sentence: 那地方离地铁口还有一段路，我们要是现在不乘车过去，等散场的人一多，外面那条小路马上就会堵住。
她原来打算乘夜里的航班赶回去参加第二天的签约，后来飞机晚点，只好连夜改成高铁加出租车。
这位老人虽然腿脚慢一点，却坚持自己乘公共汽车去医院，因为他觉得总麻烦孩子请假并不是长久办法。

example_translations.translation: That place is still some distance from the subway exit. If we do not ride there now, the little road outside will jam up as soon as the crowd leaving gets bigger.
She had planned to take a night flight back for the signing the next day, but when the plane was delayed she had to switch overnight to high-speed rail plus a taxi.
Although the old man moved a little slowly, he insisted on taking the bus to the hospital himself, because he felt it was not a long-term solution to keep making his children take time off.

glosses.notes: Here it is pronounced chéng and means holding or putting food or liquid into a container.

examples.sentence: 厨房的人看见后面排队的人越来越多，就先用大盆把刚做好的汤盛出来，免得大家一碗一碗等得太久。
母亲怕玻璃杯太烫手，特地换了个厚一点的碗来盛粥，还提醒孩子别边跑边喝。
那个人把洗好的苹果分开盛在几个小盘里，再端到前面的房间去，这样后排的人也不用一直站起来拿。

example_translations.translation: When the people in the kitchen saw the line behind getting longer and longer, they first ladled the freshly made soup into a big basin so people would not have to wait too long one bowl at a time.
Afraid the glass cup would be too hot to hold, the mother switched to a thicker bowl to hold the porridge and reminded the child not to drink while running.
That person divided the washed apples into several small plates, then carried them to the room in front, so the people in back did not have to keep standing up to take some.

glosses.notes: Used for taking responsibility for handling or organizing an event, project, or formal activity.

examples.sentence: 这次活动虽然是几家单位一起发起的，但真正承办全部现场安排的，还是那支去年办过大活动的年轻团队。
小城第一次承办这么大的比赛时，连车站的路牌和志愿者培训都提前做了好几轮，怕外地队伍一到就找不到地方。
后来他们不再随便承办临时加进来的活动，因为上一次为了赶进度，整个组都快撑不住了。

example_translations.translation: Although the event was launched jointly by several units, the team that actually undertook all the on-site arrangements was still the young group that had organized a major event the year before.

When the small city hosted such a big competition for the first time, even the station signs and volunteer training were done several rounds ahead of time, because they were afraid teams from other places would arrive and not know where to go.
Later they stopped casually taking on last-minute added activities, because the last time they rushed the schedule, the whole team was almost unable to keep going.

glosses.notes: To give punishment for wrongdoing, whether in a school, workplace, or formal system.

examples.sentence: 老师当着全班的面说，这次让他留下来整理东西不是为了惩罚谁，而是希望弄坏东西的人先学会为这件事负责。
平台更新规定以后，有人要是总拿别人的作品说成是自己的，账号不仅会被惩罚，连以前谈好的事也可能一起取消。
家长后来发现，光靠把孩子手机收走来惩罚他并没有用，真正有用的是一起订清楚晚上几点前必须把作业做完。

example_translations.translation: The teacher told the whole class that keeping him back to tidy things up this time was not meant to punish anyone, but to help the person who broke something learn to take responsibility first.

After the platform updated its rules, if someone kept taking other people’s work and claiming it was their own, not only would the account be punished, even previously agreed matters might be canceled together.

The parents later realized that simply taking away the child’s phone to punish him was not useful. What actually helped was clearly setting together what time homework had to be finished each evening.

glosses.notes: Used when a business deal, sale, or agreement is successfully concluded.

examples.sentence: 那个人原来一直嫌房子的朝向一般，看完边上新开的学校和地铁出口以后，当天下午就松口成交了。
那台机器讲了快一个小时都没人决定买，直到店里的人把以后坏了怎么办讲清楚，才一下成交了十几台。
两边价格其实差得不远，之所以一直没有成交，就是因为谁都不愿意先把运输风险写进合同里。

example_translations.translation: That person had always disliked the apartment’s direction, but after seeing the newly opened school nearby and the subway exit, he agreed to the deal that very afternoon.
People talked about that machine for almost an hour without deciding to buy it. Only after the store staff explained clearly what to do if it broke later were more than ten units sold at once.
The prices on the two sides were actually not far apart. The reason the deal still had not gone through was that neither side was willing to put the transport risk into the contract first.

glosses.notes: Used for making a clear promise or commitment, especially when responsibility or expectations are involved.

examples.sentence: 负责人在说明会上承诺，系统切换期间就算出现小故障，也会有人整夜值班处理，不会让住户第二天一早就报修无门。
他不是不想同意，只是觉得在资金和人手都还没有准备好以前，先把时间承诺出去对团队并不公平。
商家承诺七天内可以无理由退货，等顾客把东西寄回去以后，客服又开始一条一条看包装的问题。

example_translations.translation: At the briefing, the person in charge promised that even if small glitches appeared during the system switch, someone would still be on duty all night to deal with them, and residents would not find themselves unable to report problems first thing the next morning.
It was not that he did not want to agree. He just felt that before funding and staff were truly ready, making a time commitment first was not fair to the team.
The seller promised returns without reason within seven days, but after the customer sent the item back, customer service started looking at the packaging issue one point at a time.

glosses.notes: An idiom for very large numbers of people or things, especially when the scale feels overwhelming.

examples.sentence: 节日活动刚开始，河边两岸就聚起成千上万的观众，连平时走路都嫌空的桥上都站满了拿手机的人。
那段求助视频传开以后，成千上万的网友留言问仓库地址，想看看自己家里有没有能马上寄过去的厚衣服。
每到旅游的时候，这个原本安静的海边小城都会一下迎来成千上万的外地人，所以本地人买菜都得尽量早一点出门。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the holiday event began, spectators gathered by the thousands on both sides of the river, and even the bridge that usually felt empty was filled with people holding up their phones.

After that video asking for help spread, countless internet users left messages asking for the warehouse address, wanting to see whether they had heavy clothes at home that could be mailed over immediately.
Whenever the travel season comes, this normally quiet seaside town suddenly receives thousands upon thousands of people from elsewhere, so locals even have to go out early to buy vegetables.

glosses.notes: Used when something is displayed, revealed, or gradually appears in front of people.

examples.sentence: 天刚黑的时候，山路旁边的灯慢慢都亮起来，整个古镇在雾里呈现出另外一种安静又热闹的样子。
调查结果如果只看总数，问题还不明显，一按年龄和地区分开，差距就立刻呈现出来了。
导演没有急着解释人物关系，而是先让几段日常对话慢慢呈现他们之间早就有了的不满。

example_translations.translation: When it had just turned dark, the lights by the mountain road slowly all lit up, and the whole old town in the mist took on another look that was quiet yet lively.
If you look only at the total numbers in the survey results, the problem is still not obvious. But once the data is split by age and region, the gap immediately shows up.
The director did not rush to explain the characters’ relationships, but first let several everyday conversations slowly bring out the dissatisfaction that had long existed between them.

glosses.notes: Refers to the actual results or effectiveness produced by a method, policy, or period of work.

examples.sentence: 新规定到底有没有成效，不能只看第一周的数据好不好看，还得看一个月以后大家是不是真的改掉了老问题。
社区把志愿者重新分组以后，夜间检查的成效一下明显多了，连以前最常被投诉的几个路口也安静下来。
这套训练方法刚开始很累，只要坚持两个多月，成效通常会先从呼吸上慢慢看出来。

example_translations.translation: Whether the new rule has real results cannot be judged only by whether the first week’s numbers look good; we also have to see whether people have actually corrected the old problems a month later.
After the community regrouped the volunteers, the results of the night checks became much more obvious at once, and even the intersections that used to draw the most complaints grew quiet.
This training method is tiring at first, but if you stick with it for more than two months, the results usually start to show first in your breathing.

glosses.notes: Refers to the quality of being truthful, reliable, and worthy of trust in what you say and do.

examples.sentence: 老板做生意一直讲诚信，所以哪怕边上后来又开了几家更大的店，很多老顾客买贵一点也还是愿意回来找他。
招聘会上不少公司都把诚信写进要求，真正让求职的人放心的，还是面试时肯不肯把加班、合同和工资说清楚。
他觉得合作能不能长久，先看的不是对方办公室大不大，而是对方出小问题的时候有没有最基本的诚信。

example_translations.translation: The owner has always done business with honesty and trustworthiness, so even after several bigger stores opened nearby, many long-time customers were still willing to come back to him even if they had to pay a little more.

At the job fair, many companies wrote integrity into their requirements, but what truly reassured job seekers was still whether the company was willing to explain overtime, contracts, and salary clearly during the interview.
He felt that what determines whether cooperation can last is not how large the other side’s office is, but whether they show the most basic honesty when small problems come up.

glosses.notes: A fixed Chinese idiom, often four characters long, that carries a compact traditional meaning or story.

examples.sentence: 老师讲到那个成语的时候，没有急着让学生背解释，而是先讲了当年那段故事，让大家知道它为什么会这样说。
他平时说话并不爱卖弄，一到演讲比赛，合适的时候总能自然带出几个成语，所以听起来又自然又不死板。
孩子写作文最怕把成语用得太满，因为表面上看词很漂亮，一放错地方反而比普通句子更容易让人出戏。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher came to that idiom, she did not rush the students into memorizing the explanation, but first told the story behind it so everyone would know why people say it that way.
He does not usually like showing off when he speaks, but once he gets to a speech contest, he can naturally bring in a few idioms at the right moments, so he sounds natural without sounding stiff.

What children fear most in essay writing is packing in too many idioms, because on the surface the words look beautiful, but if they are placed wrongly they can pull the reader out of the writing even more easily than ordinary sentences do.

glosses.notes: A town or urban settlement, often contrasted with villages or more remote countryside areas.

examples.sentence: 高速公路修通以后，这些原来只靠一条旧路联系外面的城镇，慢慢把车站、医院和学校都办起来了。
摄影的人这次想拍的不是最热闹的大城市，而是那些天一黑商店就早早关门的小城镇里，人们怎么过普通的晚上。
暴雨连续下了两天以后，周围几个低处的城镇都开始提前转移老人和孩子，怕夜里河水突然再涨上来。

example_translations.translation: After the highway was completed, these towns that had originally been connected to the outside only by a single old road gradually managed to establish a station, a hospital, and a school.
What the photographer wanted to capture this time was not the busiest big city, but how people in those small towns where the shops close early as soon as it gets dark spend an ordinary evening.
After the heavy rain continued for two days, several low-lying towns nearby began moving elderly people and children out in advance, afraid that the river might suddenly rise again during the night.

glosses.notes: Describes something that continues for a long time without fading quickly.

examples.sentence: 这双鞋刚穿上也许没有那么软，很多人最后还是选它，就是因为走远路的时候支撑更稳定，舒服得也更持久。
讨论真正有效的合作时，经理最看重的不是一时热情，而是团队能不能保持一种持久而稳定的沟通节奏。
那场掌声并不特别响，却持续得很持久，因为台上的老演员演完以后，很多观众还舍不得立刻起身离开。

example_translations.translation: These shoes may not feel especially soft at first, but many people still choose them in the end because the support is steadier on long walks and the comfort also lasts longer.
When discussing truly effective cooperation, what the manager values most is not a burst of short-term enthusiasm, but whether the team can maintain a lasting and stable rhythm of communication.

The applause was not especially loud, but it lasted a long time, because after the veteran actor on stage finished performing, many in the audience were still reluctant to get up and leave right away.

glosses.notes: To have or possess something, especially cards, certificates, shares, or similar formal holdings.

examples.sentence: 银行通知说，持有这类旧卡的客户下个月都要重新登记信息，不然部分线上服务会暂时受到影响。
他虽然长期持有这家公司的股票，却很少在吃饭的时候劝朋友跟着买，因为他知道每个人能承受的风险完全不同。
法院后来要求平台说明，为什么还允许已经不再持有合法许可的商家继续接单营业。

example_translations.translation: The bank issued a notice saying that customers holding this type of old card would all have to register their information again next month, otherwise some online services would be temporarily affected.
Although he has held this company’s stock for a long time, he rarely urges friends to buy it too while eating together, because he knows each person can handle a completely different level of risk.
Later the court asked the platform to explain why it still allowed merchants that no longer held valid licenses to continue taking orders and operating.

glosses.notes: Can mean the traditional Chinese unit chi or a ruler used for measuring lines and lengths.

examples.sentence: 师傅量过以后说，这块板子要是再宽一尺，就能直接放在窗边用，现在这个尺寸只能先改成架子的一层。
孩子把画好的线又用尺比了一遍，发现左边果然比右边高出一点，于是擦掉重画，连老师都没提醒他。
卖布的师傅摸了摸这段布，就知道离客人要的长度还差半尺，所以一边说笑一边又慢慢往外多放一点。

example_translations.translation: After measuring it, the craftsman said that if this board were one chi wider, it could be used directly by the window, but at its current size it could only first be turned into one shelf layer.

The child checked the line he had drawn again with a ruler and found that the left side really was a little higher than the right, so he erased it and drew it again without even being reminded by the teacher.
The cloth seller felt the piece of cloth and immediately knew it was still half a chi short of the length the customer wanted, so while talking and smiling he slowly let out a little more.

glosses.notes: The size or dimensions of something, especially when checking fit, specifications, or measurements.

examples.sentence: 样品刚送到的时候，做设计的人先不是看颜色，而是拿着图纸一项一项看尺寸，怕后面大量生产以后整批都装不上去。
她在网上看中那件外套很久了，还是一直没下单，因为评论里不少人都说同样的尺寸穿起来松紧差很多。
工作人员把东西的尺寸重新量了一遍，确认确实进不了门以后，才决定先拆开外面的包装再慢慢往楼上搬。

example_translations.translation: When the sample first arrived, the person doing the design did not look at the color first, but took the drawing and checked the dimensions item by item, afraid that once full production began, the whole batch would not fit.
She had liked that coat online for a long time, but still had not placed the order, because many comments said the very same size could fit very differently.
The staff measured the item’s dimensions again and, after confirming it really could not fit through the door, decided to remove the outer packaging first and then carry it upstairs slowly.

glosses.notes: Can refer to a sudden urge to act or describe someone who acts too quickly without enough thought.

examples.sentence: 他听完那段录音以后确实很生气，但还是先出去走了一圈，怕自己带着一时的冲动回去说出更难收回的话。
年轻的时候她买东西特别冲动，一看到店里说今天最后一天就想下单，后来搬家整理柜子才知道自己花了多少没必要的钱。
比赛输了以后最难的不是接受结果，而是控制那种立刻去找裁判理论的冲动，因为一开口局面只会更乱。

example_translations.translation: After listening to that recording, he really was angry, but he still went out for a walk first, afraid that if he went back while carried by a moment of impulse, he would say something even harder to take back.

When she was younger, she was especially impulsive about shopping. The moment a store said today was the last day, she wanted to place an order, and only when moving house and cleaning out her cabinets did she realize how much unnecessary money she had spent.

After losing the match, the hardest part was not accepting the result, but controlling that impulse to go argue with the referee right away, because once he started talking, the situation would only grow messier.

glosses.notes: To strike something forcefully or to strongly affect a situation, plan, or business.

examples.sentence: 洪水最先冲击的是桥边那排旧房子下面的地，所以工作人员连夜把住在一层的几户人先送到了学校里。
这条消息一公布，就直接冲击了小店原来的进货计划，因为大家谁也没想到材料价格会在一周里连着涨两次。
新平台上线以后，最先被冲击的不是大公司，而是那些一直靠单一服务维持生意的小团队。
